Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

relatively adverb

also comparatively, fairly (for what it is), for (for those times, for a child), considering

classical

Cic. Sen. 55: senectūs est nātūrā loquācior (Lewis & Short)

loquācior, longior (comparative alone)

the comparative of an adjective or adverb without a second term

rather, relatively (talkative, long)

Latin says “relatively long” with the comparative alone, which then means “rather, fairly, more than usual”: loquācior, rather talkative.

Other words

  • ut (+ in, or a clause) — for, considering, relative to (the times, the person)

    conjunction: ut with in + ablative, or with a clause, restricting what is said · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 102: scrīptor, ut temporibus illīs, lūculentus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 12: multae, ut in homine Rōmānō, litterae (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 12.2.2: nōnnihil, ut in tantīs malīs, est prōfectum (Lewis & Short)

    The Latin for “good for those times”, “learned, for a Roman”: ut limits the praise to the circumstances (Lewis & Short, s.v. ut: “for, as, considering”).

  • prō (+ ablative) — in proportion to, relative to

    preposition with the ablative · also used · classical · Liv. 21.29: atrōcius quam prō numerō pugnantium (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 27: agere prō vīribus (Lewis & Short)

    Measures a thing against a standard: prō vīribus, as far as one’s strength allows; atrōcius quam prō numerō, fiercer than the numbers would suggest (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • senectūs est nātūrā loquācior

    old age is by nature rather talkativeCic. Sen. 55 (Lewis & Short)

  • Caelius Antipater, scrīptor, ut temporibus illīs, lūculentus

    Caelius Antipater, a fine writer for those timesCic. Brut. 102 (Lewis & Short)

  • multae, ut in homine Rōmānō, litterae

    much learning, for a RomanCic. Sen. 12 (Lewis & Short)

See also quite, slightly, more.
